title: How to Choose the Right Industrial Router for Remote Site Connectivity
description: A practical framework for selecting industrial LTE/5G routers based on environment, bandwidth requirements, redundancy needs, and fleet manageability.

content.text: Selecting an industrial router is rarely just about bandwidth. For remote and unattended sites — telecom towers, substations, solar farms, pipeline monitoring stations — the router is the single point of connectivity between the field and your operations centre. Getting the specification wrong means costly replacements, intermittent monitoring gaps, or exposure to security risk.

Industrial sites impose conditions that consumer and even enterprise networking hardware cannot withstand. Before evaluating any router, confirm its operating temperature range, ingress protection (IP) rating, and vibration tolerance.

items: Operating temperature: look for -40°C to +70°C for outdoor or unventilated cabinet deployments
IP rating: IP30 minimum for indoor cabinets; IP65 or higher for direct outdoor exposure
Humidity: 95% non-condensing is a common requirement for tropical deployments
Vibration and shock ratings matter for vehicle-mounted or heavy-industrial installations

content.text: For most remote sites, LTE is the primary WAN medium. However, the choice between LTE Cat-4, Cat-6, Cat-12, and 5G Sub-6GHz has significant cost and throughput implications. For low-bandwidth telemetry (sensor readings, alarms), Cat-4 is often sufficient. For video surveillance or high-frequency data streaming, Cat-6 or 5G becomes necessary.

content.title: Key Recommendation
content.text: Always specify dual-SIM capability. Single-SIM deployments at remote sites create a single point of failure — when the primary carrier has an outage in a rural area, there is no fallback. Dual-SIM with automatic failover eliminates this risk with minimal cost premium.

items: Hardware-based firewall with stateful packet inspection
VPN support (OpenVPN, IPSec, WireGuard) for secure tunnels back to operations centres
Certificate-based device authentication — avoid shared-key deployments at scale
Regular firmware update capability via remote management platform

content.text: When managing dozens or thousands of routers, the management platform matters as much as the device hardware. Zero-touch provisioning (ZTP), remote configuration rollout, firmware management, and real-time health dashboards are non-negotiable at scale.
